reply_text:
You're right that my wording was inconsistent, and that's my fault. Throughout the night I called the runtime "C", for example "the C runtime underneath". But much of it lives in C++ files: `object.cpp`, `io.cpp` and `apply.cpp` are C++, and they expose C-style functions. Only the inline functions in `lean.h` are actually C. So "C" was imprecise. I should have said "C/C++ runtime".

What I meant to say, and still stand by, is narrower: the **parser** isn't C++. C++ is involved in three places:

| Part | Language | Needed for a blank file? |
|---|---|---|
| Parser (grammar, tokeniser, combinators) | Lean | yes |
| Runtime primitives (strings, arrays, hashing, memory, IO) | C (`lean.h`) and C++ (`runtime/*.cpp`) | yes, and the port transcribes them in Python |
| Shell entry point (`lean_main`) | C++ | its effects only (initialisation order) |
| Loading `.olean` imports (`library/module.cpp`) | C++ | no; needed once a file has imports |
| Kernel type checker (`src/kernel`) | C++ | no; needed once declarations are checked |

So C++ was involved tonight, through the runtime. It wasn't the parser, and the kernel and import loader are the C++ still ahead.
